question: Should plugin-originated approval requests support an explicit per-request advisory timeout terminal outcome, alongside fail-closed defaults, and expose caller-supplied sanitized preview and deadline fields?
rationale: The current discussion identifies a legitimate unattended-workflow use case, but choosing whether this becomes a permanent Plugin SDK capability determines both execution authority and long-term compatibility.

options.title: Approve explicit advisory outcomes
options.body: Keep fail-closed as the default but define a bounded, recorded per-request advisory timeout terminal outcome and the allowed plugin request fields.

options.title: Fail closed universally
options.body: Retire allow-on-timeout semantics for all plugin approval requests and require advisory workflows to use another non-authorizing mechanism.

options.title: Defer Plugin SDK expansion
options.body: Keep the durable lifecycle internal to existing approval gates until a separate SDK design is approved.

recommendation.title: Approve explicit advisory outcomes
recommendation.body: Keep fail-closed as the default but define a bounded, recorded per-request advisory timeout terminal outcome and the allowed plugin request fields.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor carried the merged lifecycle across the gateway, channel, UI, native, and ancestor-projection boundaries that the remaining API policy would extend.
